# Goban Studio v9.0.0

v9 is rebuilt around one loop: **play a game → see what mattered, on the
board → try that moment again → play the next game**. Two spaces instead
of four, one opponent choice, one record of how you play, and much less on
every screen.

## Before you update: v9 starts empty

v9 does not read anything saved by earlier versions: your games, progress,
rating and settings stay behind. **To keep a game, export it as SGF in v8
first** (open it, then Export SGF); v9 can import SGF files. A v8 backup
file cannot be imported into v9.

`SHA256SUMS` lists the checksums of every file. Windows on ARM runs the x64
build under the system's emulation.

## Two spaces

- **Play** opens on your game in progress, or on the game suggested for
  you with one button: 9×9 for a beginner, 19×19 from about 20 kyu, the
  other board as a quiet link. Below it are your level, your games, the
  classics and the opening explorer.
- **Learn** opens on one short path for today, chosen for you and played
  as one session. It holds the next lesson, your own mistakes and the
  problems due for review, this week's focus (named, with its reason), one
  stretch problem and new problems at your level; for beginners, capture
  Go and a first 9×9 game too. Each row says why it is there. When you
  are done, it says so and stops. A restart keeps what you did today.
  Every lesson and problem stays one row away, in the catalog.

## The review is on the board

- When a game ends, its board becomes the review — no separate report
  page. It shows the result and your rating change, the balance of the
  game, the three phases (with KataGo), up to three key moments with
  their stories, and your comments and variations, together with image
  and SGF export.
- **Try again from the position.** Each key moment of your own game can be
  replayed: the board goes back to the position, you play a new move, and
  KataGo judges it on the spot. A miss shows KataGo's move and comes back
  in Learn on the spaced-review ladder.
- One analysis per game, kept with the game. Your games without a review
  are analysed quietly in the background, and the computer's move always
  comes first.

## One opponent choice

New game asks for one thing: strength, as a measured rank from 30 kyu to
7 dan. The app plays it with whichever KataGo setting measured closest
— human-style where that measured well — and shows the rank it actually
plays. There are no modes to choose. Without the optional networks the
ladder ends at 4 dan.

## One record of how you play

Your rating, your mistakes, your problems and lessons, and this week's
focus now live in one model. The teaching warnings, the suggested game,
the review and Learn all read it, so they always agree.

## Less, and faster

- Removed:
  - the 40 pro-opening guess drills (the explorer covers openings);
  - "guess the next move";
  - board materials and flat stones (one board look);
  - importing SGF problem collections;
  - the strength chart (your level is one number with its ±);
  - the "this week" counts;
  - Today, the Practice page, the Library page, the report page,
    *Analyse all* and the background-work list.
- The app script is 1.0 MB instead of 2.2 MB in v8. Lessons, problems and
  classic records load after start-up, when first needed.

## Your data

- Everything is kept as files in the app's data folder, one per game. Each
  file is written whole (written beside, then swapped in), and there is no
  size limit.
- *Export backup* in Settings writes everything as one file; *Import
  backup* puts it back.

## Fixes

- Back from a lesson or problem of today's path returns to it inside the
  path.
- A beginner is no longer offered an hour-long 19×19 game first.
- A test-suite flaw that let one file's timers reach the next file's fake
  engine was fixed; it had caused rare false failures.

## Known limits

- **No data from earlier versions is read** (see the top of these notes).
- The builds are not code-signed (no certificates yet). The update
  checksum guards against damaged or wrong downloads; it is not a
  signature.
- Not yet checked by people: a usability test of the new two-space layout,
  a strong player's review of the course, a native-speaker review of the
  Chinese, Korean and Japanese text, and a real screen-reader session.
- *Try again* needs KataGo (the desktop app); the browser preview has no
  KataGo.
- The KataGo check of the course leaves some steps for a human (rule
  steps, small shape boards, endgame boards with open areas, one 3-3
  joseki step).
- 13×13 handicap games were not measured; the standard ladder's 10-kyu
  anchor was not measured again.
- The counting solver ignores ko threats; endgame problems avoid ko.
